study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology in violence, psychosis, and psychopathy

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Normative models based on large lifespan reference data were used to map individual-level deviations in cortical thickness, surface area, and subcortical volumes among men with schizophrenia spectrum disorders with and without a history of severe violence and violent men without schizophrenia, and to test group differences and associations with psychopathy traits.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: BrainChart pre-trained normative models (multi-site, 82 sites); Local HC calibration set (TOP; uTOP; STROKEMRI; sTOP)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The study applied pre-trained normative models from the BrainChart project and used an unmatched local healthy control set to calibrate (fine-tune) the model to unseen scanners. Participants (including HCs) were recruited from four Oslo-based studies (TOP, uTOP, STROKEMRI, sTOP).

STROKEMRI ... uTOP ... sTOP ..."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: GLM via PALM with 10,000 permutations; dependent variable = ROI deviation scores; predictors = PCL-R total, age, psychosis status, and ICV (for area/volume); multiple comparisons controlled with FWE/FDR as specified; groups matched by age and scanner using R matchIt for group contrasts
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Heterogeneous individual deviation patterns across groups; SSD-V showed elevated extreme negative deviations particularly in collateral transverse sulcus, lingual gyrus, and cerebellum; SSD-NV and nonSSD-V showed distinct regional patterns; no significant associations with psychopathy after multiple-comparison correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: All clinical groups exhibited higher frequencies of extreme negative deviations in cortical area and subcortical volume relative to HC, but not in cortical thickness. Significant group differences in deviation scores were observed in select ROIs after multiple-comparison correction (e.g., left inferior lateral ventricle and pallidum volumes for SSD-NV vs HC; cerebellar white matter/cortex and left subcallosal area/thickness for SSD-V vs HC). SSD-V showed more extreme negative deviations in collateral sulci regions and left lingual gyrus; SSD-NV showed more in parieto‑occipital and suborbital sulci; nonSSD-V in paracentral and middle frontal regions. No significant PCL-R associations remained after correction.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Small N in violent groups; male-only sample; no control for cumulative antipsychotic exposure; potential residual substance-use effects; cross-sectional design limits inference; atlas-level ROI analyses may under-represent true associations vs vertex-wise analyses; violence defined as lifetime binary narrower than WHO definition.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: "The study has some limitations. The relatively small number of subjects with a history of violence, as well as the male only sample ... might limit the generalizability ... the models were not corrected for substance use ... we did not control for cumulative effects of antipsychotic medication ... The most severely ill or aggressive persons ... were not eligible ... Violence was defined as a lifetime binary variable which was narrower than the WHO definition ... an inherent limitation in all crosssectional neuroimaging studies ..."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Demonstrates feasibility of normative modeling in forensic psychiatry; individual-level deviation maps may inform clinicians and forensic experts and potentially guide targeted treatments.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: HC_N refers to the unmatched local calibration set (n=998) used to fine-tune pre-trained BrainChart models to unseen scanners. Age statistics for this calibration HC set were not reported; matched HC (n=196) age summary is provided. Pre-training cohort size/age range (N=58,835; 2–100 years; 82 sites) reported for model origin. All analyzed clinical participants were male.
